solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: One scrambled egg followed by a pee, of no consequence to Ronnie Wood?

definitions.text: of no consequence to Ronnie Wood
definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer rather than a noun for it; the question mark flags the looseness

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are stirred into a mess, so these letters are stirred out of order too

blocks.note: one is a, the indefinite article
taken as written
taken as written
pee is how the letter P is said, and also slang for a penny

explanation.surface: A crude breakfast-and-toilet joke turning into a dig at a rock star's love life.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolling Stones guitarist Ronnie Wood married a woman over thirty years younger than him, so a big difference in years clearly didn't bother him.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a difference in years between partners, which the guitarist's marriage to a much younger woman shows he shrugged off.

clue.text: Left wing group takes little time getting males on corporation

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
males are men
corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A left-wing faction gains men and a corporation, as if taking over business.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation here is the jocular word for a large stomach, not a company. In a down clue, 'males on corporation' puts the men above the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the campaigning organisation founded to back Jeremy Corbyn's leadership inside the Labour Party.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Markle's mixed up with EC leaders – fishy, that

definitions.note: a phrase meaning 'that is a fish', pointing at a noun

indicators.note: things mixed up are jumbled together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the European Commission's leadership, abbreviated EC

explanation.surface: Meghan Markle tangled up with European bigwigs, and the whole affair smells suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' looks like it means suspicious; read with 'that' it means the thing described is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The mackerel is a common striped sea fish, so the answer is literally something fishy.

clue.text: "Just Victory. Good Crowd" – Daily Mail etc.

blocks.note: just means fair or right
a victory is a win
G is the abbreviation for good
a press is a crowd or throng of people

explanation.surface: A triumphant tabloid headline, the kind the Daily Mail might run.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised words read like a headline; each is a separate piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mail is a conservative British newspaper, an example of the newspapers on the political right.

clue.text: C-Cyclops pinched by crap fastener

indicators.note: something pinched is gripped between two sides, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: grot is British slang for rubbish or junk
Cyclops is the setter, so 'me'; the stammered initial is copied, giving a stuttered 'me'

explanation.surface: The setter stammers his own name while being nicked by some rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself means ME; the stutter in 'C-Cyclops' tells you to stutter that ME too, doubling its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet ring used to reinforce a hole that a cord or fastening passes through.

clue.text: Harry, for instance? Yes and no

definitions.text: Harry, for instance? Yes and no

blocks.note: surface: Prince Harry as an example of something
setter's reading: 'any Tom, Dick or Harry' is an ordinary bloke, which Prince Harry both is and is not

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'any Tom, Dick or Harry' means any ordinary person, so a Harry is typical; but the famous Harry is a royal, hardly typical, hence 'yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an ordinary average citizen, whose views stand for public opinion.

clue.text: Johnson famously gets one by balls – perverse

indicators.note: perverse means turned the wrong way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: one is a, the indefinite article
by way of is via
balls is slang for nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson gets hold of someone by the testicles, a perverse image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson' suggests Boris, but the famous Johnson meant is Amy Johnson, the pioneering 1930s pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Johnson was the first woman to fly solo from Britain to Australia, so she is best known as a pilot.

clue.text: Source of apple tart turned up in US city

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only its opening letter is used
in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first letter of apple
tart is slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: An apple tart turns up somewhere in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple tart' reads as a pudding, but tart is the insulting word for a woman, and the two pieces flip together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in the state of Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: Buzz allowed to be a hairy thing

blocks.note: to give someone a buzz is to give them a ring on the phone
allowed means let

explanation.surface: Something buzzing is permitted to be hairy, like an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' suggests a bee or noise, but it is a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiralling curl of hair, so it is quite literally a thing made of hair.

clue.text: Bill wants politician to withdraw

blocks.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party
to back off or back away is to withdraw

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation needs a politician to pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like parliamentary legislation or a man's name, but it is a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenback is American slang for a dollar banknote, named for the colour of its reverse side.

clue.text: Brothel entrance has classical beauty

indicators.note: what a phrase has, it contains, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A woman at the door of a brothel is a classic beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of 'Brothel' and the start of 'entrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy, in Greek myth, was the most beautiful woman in the world, her face launching a thousand ships.

clue.text: Leader elected after fix?

indicators.note: coming after means following in line, so the piece named first is placed second

blocks.note: to fix something in place is to put it there
a party elected is in, as in voted in

explanation.surface: A leader who wins an election only after rigging it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' hints at a rigged vote, a joke at the Russian president's expense; in the wordplay it simply means put.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Putin is the long-serving president of Russia, its head of state and ruler.

clue.text: Sod the party crackpot

blocks.note: 'sod it' and 'screw it' are the same dismissive curse
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Someone cursing the party as a nutter's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod is a mild British curse; here it swaps for its equivalent, screw.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball is chiefly American slang for an eccentric or crazy person, the same as a crackpot.

clue.text: Maine politician belonging to 'the man's city'

blocks.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
an MP is a Member of Parliament
something of the man's is his

explanation.surface: A politician from Maine belongs to some big man's city.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'the man's city' look like a name; the possessive is a piece on its own and only 'city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Memphis is a Tennessee city on the Mississippi, and also the ancient capital of Egypt.

clue.text: Mean Conservative gains Joanna's heart

blocks.note: a mean is the middle value
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A stingy Tory wins a woman named Joanna's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (from 'pianna'), not a woman; 'Mean' is the average, not stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the note near the centre of the piano keyboard, so it sits at the instrument's heart.

clue.text: Shambolic BHS involved with Boris (having changed political sides)

indicators.note: switching from right to left in politics means swapping R for L in a word
involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written; BHS was the British Home Stores chain
the name with its R (right) changed to L (left)

explanation.surface: The chaotic collapse of the BHS stores dragged in Boris, who has switched parties.
explanation.walkthrough: BHS, British Home Stores, was a department store chain whose 2016 collapse was a scandal. R and L stand for right and left, so changing sides swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slobbish is untidy and messy in habits, which is what shambolic describes.

clue.text: Artistic print: sod all about sod all – shred!

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: sod all is British slang for nothing, nil
nothing again, this time as the zero-shaped letter O
to shred is to cut up

explanation.surface: An angry rant about a worthless artistic print: tear it up!
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'sod all' gives two different forms of nothing: the word nil, turned round, and the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a design carved into a block of linoleum, an art printmaking technique.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Act desperately, grab ex-Labour minister by balls, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of a word, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: to grab is to clutch
by and at both mean next to, as in 'by the door'
Jack Straw was Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary under Tony Blair
the last letter of balls

explanation.surface: A desperate act: seizing a former Labour minister by the testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By balls' reads as the grip on the minister, but 'by' gives its own piece and 'balls, finally' is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes grabbing at any small hope, however feeble, when in a hopeless situation, like a drowning person.

clue.text: Prepare for a Friday at work and give someone a bollocking

definitions.text: Prepare for a Friday at work

blocks.clueFragment: Prepare for a Friday at work
blocks.note: first meaning: wear casual clothes, as on an office's casual Friday
second meaning: scold someone severely

explanation.surface: Getting ready for the end of the working week and then tearing a strip off someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A bollocking is a British slang telling-off. Many offices have a casual-clothes Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both wearing informal clothing and reprimanding someone harshly.

clue.text: I agree to get screwed without a peak

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped
something screwed is twisted out of shape, so the letters are twisted round

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: Someone consents to be cheated, or to a crude sexual proposition, with no summit in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A peak' looks like the definition, but the a is the letter removed, leaving 'peak' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous mountain in the Swiss Alps, known for its deadly north face.

clue.text: Doin' it without holding ass

indicators.note: what is holding something has it inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run through the three words

explanation.surface: A crude picture of having sex without grabbing a bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' looks like a backside in the surface, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a stupid person, and a nitwit is likewise a silly fool.

clue.text: 1/500th of a monkey's enclosure

blocks.note: first meaning: a monkey is British slang for £500, so a five-hundredth is the basic British money unit
second meaning: a pen where stray animals or impounded cars are kept

explanation.surface: A tiny fraction of a monkey's cage at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkey is British slang for £500; the surface makes you think of the animal and its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the British unit of money and a pen for strays or confiscated vehicles.

clue.text: Possibly McDonnell's task to stifle sources of external pressure

indicators.note: sources are where things begin, so the opening letters are used
to stifle is to smother, wrapping one thing around another

blocks.note: a task is a duty
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Labour's John McDonnell has the job of resisting outside pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: John McDonnell was Jeremy Corbyn's shadow chancellor and closest ally, effectively his second-in-command; 'possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is a second-in-command who stands in for a leader, a role McDonnell was seen to play for Corbyn.

clue.text: Carry Brenda's foreign piece

blocks.note: to lug is to carry something heavy
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a friend's souvenir from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina. Piece is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol, and piece is slang for a handgun, so it is a gun from abroad.

clue.text: Goat nestling up to bit of bra, flower?

blocks.note: a goat butts, so it is a butter
a bra is made of two cups

explanation.surface: A goat nuzzling against part of a bra, and is that a flower?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat' is turned into what a goat does: one that butts is a butter.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common wild plant with small, glossy yellow blooms found in meadows.

clue.text: Before sex, Jeremy's half ready for underwear

blocks.note: the first half of Corbyn, surname of Labour leader Jeremy
ready means set, as in 'ready, steady, go'
S used as a short form of sex

explanation.surface: Half of Jeremy Corbyn is ready for sex, dressed in lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces of Corbyn and ready come before the sex letter. Sex as S is a loose abbreviation, not a standard one.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets are close-fitting boned garments worn under clothes to shape the waist, a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Flash Brown's in this month

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: inst. is the old business-letter abbreviation meaning of the current month
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown makes a showy appearance this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' suggests former Prime Minister Gordon Brown, but it is the colour. Old business letters wrote 'the 5th inst.' for the 5th of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is a split second, the same as an instant, a moment too brief to measure.
